prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions, and setting. Use specific action verbs and name clear maneuvers (e.g., walking, running, pushing, mopping, juggling); avoid vague verbs like "gestures"—when a gesture is visible, use a precise verb (pointing, waving, beckoning, touching, holding up) and state which body part and the gesture’s direction and intended target (e.g., "pointing with his right index finger toward the vendor"). Indicate movement directions relative to the camera/frame using a consistent order—horizontal first (toward the camera / away from the camera / left-to-right / right-to-left / past) then vertical (upward / downward)—and state whether multiple motions are simultaneous or sequential. Describe body posture with concrete observable terms (standing, seated, crouching, slightly leaning forward/back, mid-jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) and note effort or grip when evident (straining, holding with both hands). Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow) and always specify gaze targets (e.g., "eyes looking up at the kite," "gaze fixed on the camera," "looking past the crowd"). Specify precise spatial relationships, scale, and proximity (next to, behind, in front of, atop, touching, a few feet/meters apart, clustered closely, spread apart, in a line) and clarify each subject’s position relative to others and to background elements (e.g., "a third person seated at the far end," "man across from him," "behind a weathered orange wall"). Describe number and arrangement of people and audience engagement using observable cues (seated in rows, leaning forward, heads turned toward the speaker). Describe lighting and shadows with observable cues—light quality (diffuse/overcast, directional backlight, strong side light), where shadows fall and approximate shadow direction or length (casting long shadows toward the lower left). Include visible surface textures or effects when present (wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, motion blur, dust). Keep the caption concrete and image‑centered, avoid speculation, inferred intentions, or subjective judgments, and output exactly one single sentence (no lists, tags, multiple candidates, metadata, or line breaks).
